correctness.rationale: For each finite irreducible chain the stationary law and centered Poisson equation are uniquely defined. Explicit reflection lumping yields 2x2 and 3x3 generators. Reconstructing stationary laws, quasipotentials and their exact temperature derivatives yields the stated positive rational functions. Direct derivative factorization proves that the two-site response has one interior optimum iff q>sqrt(5+2sqrt6), while the three-site derivative is a strictly decreasing quadratic in alpha with positive intercept iff 3q^8-7q^6-64q^4-7q^2+3>0; a reciprocal-polynomial reduction gives the unique q3 threshold. Exact full-generator SymPy identities and ten independent finite-temperature perturbation / integrated semigroup heat checks were actually executed and passed. All statements are for m=2 or 3, f,T,alpha>0 with unit temperature-independent hopping prefactor; numerical finite checks are auxiliary only.

value.rationale: The observable (nonequilibrium excess-heat capacity) and control parameter (tumbling/persistence rate) are directly motivated by active-matter calorimetry. Exact site-dependent threshold separation establishes when the expected persistence peak does and does not exist, not merely a fixed-rate numeric value. The three-vs-two-site interval provides a natural minimal-system boundary and testable finite-chain criterion; it avoids claiming a thermodynamic transition or downstream theorem.
